title: 옷차림 동사: 입어요? 신어요? 써요? 껴요?
objective: By the end, you can choose the right verb (입다, 신다, 쓰다, 끼다, 벗다) for clothes, shoes, hats, glasses and gloves, and use it in a short -어요 sentence.
summary: Korean uses different verbs for "wear" depending on what you put on and where it goes on your body.

task.title: Choose and use verbs
task.line: Look at the item in each sentence, then choose or write the verb that matches it.

words.meaning: to wear, put on (clothes on the body) — 입어요
words.exampleMeaning: I wear jeans when I go to school.

words.meaning: to wear, put on (shoes or socks) — 신어요
words.exampleMeaning: I put on sneakers and go to the park.

words.meaning: to wear, put on (a hat or glasses, on the head or face) — 써요
words.example: 저는 컴퓨터를 할 때 안경을 써요.
words.exampleMeaning: I wear glasses when I use the computer.

words.meaning: to wear, put on (gloves or a ring, on the hands) — 껴요
to take off (clothes, shoes, a hat, glasses, gloves) — 벗어요
words.exampleMeaning: Are you hot? Then take off your coat.
I don't have my glasses. I can't see well.
The shoes are a little small.
I lost my gloves on the subway.

exercises: Choose the right verb (구두 = dress shoes): ① 바지를 (입어요 / 신어요) ② 구두를 (입어요 / 신어요) ③ 모자를 (써요 / 껴요)
Choose the one item that goes with 껴요: 모자 / 장갑 / 치마
Fill in the blank with the opposite of 써요: 교실에서는 모자를 ____.
Find the wrong verb and write the correct one: 우리 형은 모자를 신어요.
Put the words in the right order: 들어가요 / 신발을 / 벗고
answers: ① 입어요 ② 신어요 ③ 써요
